title: The Ide dialect
description: Ide is one Igbo dialect, not a language of its own — a fusion of Central and Northern Anambra speech, and an average Anambra person understands it. Its base is the Ọmambala and Idemmili dialects with Onicha, Nkpor, Nri, Enuani and Ukwuani; its voice is Idemmili. What makes it distinct is its borrowed layer, the non-Igbo words it took from Igala, Fulfulde, Kanuri, Tiv, Idoma and Ekoi.
html:
NON-IGBO WORDS

The borrowed layer

The dialect is Igbo in its base and its voice. Its distinctness comes from the words it took from the non-Igbo languages it lives among — and those words are listed one by one on the Odiana and Library pages.

EGWU EDE

The music

The Ide register, egwu ede, is a mixture of egwu ekpili, Cape Verdean morna, the Oumou Sangare manner, and Sahelian influence — the Igbo sound, the Sahel, and the West African islands in one register. The instruments that carry it are on the What is made page.

THE SOUND RULES

The sound

gh → y

A source gh is written y

agha becomes aya; Mkpọọ jàghe becomes jaye.

Read→
r → l

A source r is written l

were becomes weli; afere becomes afele.

Read→
h → f / v

A source h is f, and the North writes it v

The shift /ɦ/ → /f/ → /v/ is where Anambra North and Central fuse: afịa and avịa are one word.

Read→
(N)(C)V

Every syllable

An optional nasal, an optional consonant, a vowel. No closed syllable, ever.

Read→
chi / si

chi is the word; si is how it is said

The personal force is <code>chi</code> — also, and widely, <code>si</code> / <code>sị</code>.
